2609.29095.title: Where Does Exactly-Once Live? Model, Harness, and Tool-Contract Effects on Duplicate Side Effects in LLM Agents
2609.29095.paper_summary: When a tool-using agent's write times out or returns a server error, the action may already have taken effect. Retrying blindly duplicates it -- a second charge, a second announcement, a second deployment -- while giving up skips required work. We ask where exactly-once behaviour should be enforced: in the model, in the agent harness, or in the tool contract. We introduce LIMBO, a deterministic sandbox of six services with realistic contracts (optional idempotency keys, eventually consistent and missing read paths) and twelve fault modes injected at the service boundary, including late commits, redelivery and partial batches; every episode is graded against a ledger of committed effects. Across 25,930 episodes spanning nine recent models, three production agent harnesses, two contract variants and fifteen recovery conditions, the answer depends on the fault. When an immediate read-back can reveal what happened, the model decides: frontier models instructed to act exactly once almost never duplicate a write whose acknowledgement was lost (0.5%), weaker models often do, and the model explains 53% of the explained variance. When it cannot -- the request is still in flight, or the transport delivered it twice -- the same frontier models duplicate in 56% and 74% of episodes, and the contract explains 81%. We prove that no verification-only policy is exactly-once under late commits without a bound on in-flight time. Waiting works when such a bound is short and known, but with heavy-tailed in-flight delays even an hour of waiting per episode falls short of offering an idempotency key on every write, which lowers the duplicate rate from 28% to 4% because agents use keys when they exist. The harness barely matters, a guard that attaches keys transfers across harnesses unchanged, and agents reported success in 90% of the episodes in which they had duplicated an effect.
2609.29095.paper_summary_zh: 當一個使用工具的代理的寫入超時或返回伺服器錯誤時，該行動可能已經生效。盲目重試會重複它——第二次收費、第二次公告、第二次部署——而放棄則跳過了必要的工作。我們詢問確切應該在哪裡強制執行一次性行為：在模型中、在代理的工具中，還是在工具合約中。我們介紹了 LIMBO，一個具有六個服務的確定性沙盒，擁有現實的合約（可選的冪等鍵、最終一致和缺失的讀取路徑）以及在服務邊界注入的十二種故障模式，包括延遲提交、重新交付和部分批次；每個事件都根據已提交效果的賬本進行評分。在跨越九個最近模型、三個生產代理工具、兩個合約變體和十五個恢復條件的 25,930 個事件中，答案取決於故障。當立即回讀可以揭示發生了什麼時，模型會決定：被指示精確執行一次的前沿模型幾乎從不重複確認丟失的寫入（0.5%），較弱的模型則常常會，模型解釋了 53% 的解釋變異性。當無法做到這一點時——請求仍在傳輸中，或傳輸重複交付——相同的前沿模型在 56% 和 74% 的事件中重複，而合約解釋了 81%。我們證明，沒有驗證僅的政策在延遲提交下是無法實現一次性的，且沒有對在途時間的限制。當這樣的限制較短且已知時，等待是有效的，但在重尾的在途延遲下，即使每個事件等待一小時也無法在每次寫入上提供冪等鍵，這將重複率從 28% 降低到 4%，因為代理在存在鍵時會使用它們。工具幾乎不重要，附加鍵的保護裝置在工具之間轉移時不變，代理在 90% 的重複效果的事件中報告成功。
2609.29095.author: Jiapeng Li et.al.
